Build a level-of-detail pyramid of A5 cells

Source: R/pyramid.R
a5_pyramid.Rd

a5_pyramid() aggregates A5 cells at one resolution, the leaves, to coarser levels of detail (LODs) and returns every level as rows of one tibble. a5_write_pyramid() builds the same pyramid and writes it to a Parquet file laid out for browser rendering.

Usage

a5_pyramid(
  x,
  ...,
  lods = NULL,
  aggregate = c("mean", "rep_child"),
  reducers = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  types = NULL,
  threads = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame with one a5R::a5_cell column, or an a5R::a5_cell vector. The cells must share one resolution and appear once each; rows with NA cells are dropped. An a5R::a5_covering holds cells at mixed resolutions: convert it with a5R::a5_uncompact() first.

...

<tidy-select> Value columns to carry into the pyramid. Default: every numeric column other than the cells.

lods

Integer vector of the coarser LODs to build, each below the leaves' resolution; the leaves are always kept. Default: every resolution from 2 up to the leaves'. Resolutions 0 and 1 hold the 12 and 60 largest cells, which no map view draws.

aggregate

The reducer for every value column: "mean" (default) or "rep_child". See "Reducers".

reducers

Named character vector of reducers for single columns, overriding aggregate, such as c(count = "sum", class = "mode").

weights

Name of a numeric column of non-negative leaf weights for "mean", "mode" and "rep_child", such as the npix column from a5px::a5_read_raster(). NA weights count as 0, and leaves with weight 0 do not count. Default NULL: every leaf counts once.

types

Named character vector of storage types for single columns, such as c(red = "uint8", ndvi = "float32"). See "Column types".

threads

Number of threads, or NULL (default) for a5pyramid_threads().

Value

A tibble with one row per cell of every level, in ascending LOD and then cell id order:

  • cell: the cell, an a5R::a5_cell.

  • lod: its LOD (A5 resolution), an integer.

  • ncell: the number of leaves it summarises (1 for the leaves).

  • the value columns, integer for the integer types up to "uint16" and double otherwise.

Levels

A cell at LOD r summarises the leaves whose centres it contains, as given by a5R::a5_cell_to_supercell(), so each level partitions the leaves, and ncell counts the leaves in each cell. Supercells do not chain: a leaf's supercell two resolutions up is often not the supercell of its supercell one resolution up. Each level is therefore grouped from the leaves directly, never from the level below, and matches a5px::a5_aggregate() of the leaves to that resolution.

Reducers

Each value column is reduced over the leaves under each coarser cell by its reducer, aggregate unless reducers names another:

  • "mean": the mean, weighted by weights when given.

  • "sum", "min", "max": the sum, minimum or maximum.

  • "mode": the most frequent value, by total weight when weights is given, ties going to the smallest value. For category codes.

  • "rep_child": the value of the representative leaf, the leaf closest to the cell's mean over all "rep_child" columns, each scaled by its standard deviation over the leaves so that units do not matter. Every "rep_child" column takes its value from the same leaf, so a coarse cell keeps a combination of values that occurs in the data, such as an RGB colour, rather than a blend.

Missing values are skipped, and a cell whose leaves are all missing is NA. The weights column, when selected, is summed unless reducers says otherwise. Results do not depend on the number of threads.

Column types

Every level is stored with one schema, so each value column has one storage type, set by types: "int8", "int16", "int32", "uint8", "uint16", "uint32", "float32" or "float64". Integer columns default to "int32" and double columns to "float64". Values, leaves included, are stored as their type: an integer type rounds half to even (as round() does) and clamps to its range, so the mean of a "uint8" colour channel is a valid channel, and "float32" rounds to single precision. a5_pyramid() returns the stored values. For a browser, "uint8" suits colour channels and "float32" halves the size of continuous values.

See also

a5_write_pyramid() to write the pyramid for a browser.

Examples

library(a5R)
#> a5R 1.0.0.9000 • a5 crate 1.0.0 • A5 index 1.0 • 1 thread
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 3000), resolution = 15)
x <- data.frame(cell = cells, value = seq_along(cells))

p <- a5_pyramid(x, lods = c(9, 11, 13))
p
#> # A tibble: 1,110 × 4
#>    cell               lod ncell value
#>    <a5_cell>        <int> <int> <int>
#>  1 6316020000000000     9   441   777
#>  2 63bb920000000000     9    88   192
#>  3 63bb960000000000     9   495   334
#>  4 63bb93a000000000    11    64   701
#>  5 63bb942000000000    11   187   135
#>  6 63bb946000000000    11   187   378
#>  7 63bb94a000000000    11   261   591
#>  8 63bb94e000000000    11   192   819
#>  9 63bb952000000000    11    64   957
#> 10 63bb96e000000000    11    69   164
#> # ℹ 1,100 more rows
table(p$lod)
#> 
#>    9   11   13   15 
#>    3    7   76 1024 

# a colour composite: coarse cells keep a real colour, not a blend
x$red <- sample(0:255, nrow(x), replace = TRUE)
x$green <- sample(0:255, nrow(x), replace = TRUE)
a5_pyramid(
  x, red, green,
  aggregate = "rep_child",
  types = c(red = "uint8", green = "uint8")
)
#> # A tibble: 1,426 × 5
#>    cell               lod ncell   red green
#>    <a5_cell>        <int> <int> <int> <int>
#>  1 0c80000000000000     2  1024   126   122
#>  2 6320000000000000     3  1024   126   122
#>  3 6318000000000000     4  1024   126   122
#>  4 6316000000000000     5  1024   126   122
#>  5 63bb800000000000     6  1002   126   122
#>  6 63be800000000000     6    22   123   190
#>  7 6316200000000000     7   467   128   131
#>  8 63bba00000000000     7   557   126   122
#>  9 6316080000000000     8   467   128   131
#> 10 63bb980000000000     8   557   126   122
#> # ℹ 1,416 more rows
